agentCan: Build the Login Kit authorization flow and server-side token exchange/refresh/revoke
Prepare the sandbox demonstration (every selected product and scope visibly exercised) for the review submission

approval.cost: No fee for registration, review, or the audit is stated anywhere in the documentation read
approval.trigger: Review is required before any external user can connect in production. 'To integrate with our products, you must connect your app to TikTok for Developers and submit your app registration for review', and 'Before you integrate with our developer products, you must submit your app for review.' The Production version 'must be submitted for review to be released to the public.' Statuses: Draft > In review ('No further changes can be made at this stage'; you may Recall to withdraw) > Live or Not approved (review comments with suggested actions; fix and resubmit). What review examines (App Review Guidelines): custom app name (must match your app/website, must not reference social-media company names), clear icon, a real description, a valid official website that is not just a landing/login page, Privacy Policy and Terms of Service links visible on the website without opening a menu, platform requirements (iOS apps must be published in the Apple App Store; Android apps in the Google Play Store), and scope discipline ('Only request permissions and features that your app needs'). Two hard rejections: 'Apps must not be for private or personal use' and 'Apps that are still in development or testing will not be approved.' Pre-approval, the app is Draft and can only be exercised in Sandbox mode: 'You can create up to 5 sandboxes' per app and add 'up to 10 accounts' as target users (a target user must be a TikTok account you can log in to and must agree to the TikTok Developer Terms of Service; 'Results may take up to an hour to show after you refresh the page'). Sandbox also lacks Content Posting API for public videos and the Data Portability API. There is no public app directory/listing; approval makes your integrations Live for distribution through your own product. A SEPARATE second gate applies to posting: 'All content posted by unaudited clients will be restricted to private viewing mode... your API client must undergo an audit to verify compliance with our Terms of Service' before public posting.
approval.wait: Not stated ('TikTok for Developers will start reviewing your app once it is submitted'; no duration is published)

blockers.detail: No production users until the app is Live, and you cannot demonstrate the integration in production for the review: first-time submissions must demo from a sandbox, with every selected product and scope visibly exercised, or 'it will delay the review result'. Submission materials: 'A detailed explanation of how each product and scope works within your app or website', plus 'At least one demo video that shows the complete end-to-end flow of the up-to-date integrations' (maximum 5 videos, up to 50 MB each).
blockers.howToClear: Build the sandbox demonstration as a deliverable in its own right and request only the scopes you can show working.
blockers.title: The review gate is absolute and front-loaded

blockers.detail: While In review you cannot change anything; after approval, every change (new scope, new product, changed URLs) goes through Create revision > edit the cloned Draft > submit for review again: 'any subsequent changes must be submitted for review and approved to appear in the live release'.
blockers.howToClear: Freeze scope and product choices before submitting; batch future changes into deliberate revisions.
blockers.title: Live configuration is effectively frozen

blockers.detail: App review gets you Live, but public posting additionally requires passing the Content Posting API audit; until then everything you post is forced to private viewing mode. This is separate from the app review.
blockers.howToClear: Plan the audit as a second milestone if your product posts publicly on users' behalf.
blockers.title: Two different approvals for posting

flavor.recommended: A Web app with Login Kit, authorization code flow, and server-side token exchange, starting with user.info.basic and adding only the scopes each feature needs
flavor.why: The object is an app registered on developers.tiktok.com (owned by an organization, recommended, or an individual developer account), with a Client key and Client secret ('the unique identification key provisioned to the partner'; TikTok says client key, not client ID). Capabilities are added per app as products (Login Kit, Display API, Content Posting API, Share Kit) and scopes. 'Login Kit is based on OAuth 2.0 for user authorization and API authentication.' Login Kit is the authentication/consent product; scopes are the permissions: user.info.basic (avatar + display name) 'is the baseline' and 'will be added by default for all apps with Login Kit'; 'Anything beyond that requires pre-approval in your app configuration', and 'applying and being approved for a scope alone does not give you access to a user's data. Each user must also authorize your app.' Further scopes include user.info.profile, user.info.stats, video.list, video.upload (draft), and video.publish (direct post). Web is a confidential client: PKCE is NOT used on web (state provides CSRF protection); PKCE is required on Desktop, iOS, and Android.

Register the app and complete App details (icon 1024x1024, name, category, description, platform configuration)
Add products and scopes; configure at least one redirect URI for Login Kit
Verify URL properties for production (Terms of Service URL, Privacy Policy URL, Web/Desktop URL) via domain verification or the signature file
Import the sandbox configuration into a Production Draft, complete the App review section (per-product/scope explanations + demo video), and submit for review
name: TikTok
nuances: Tokens: access tokens are 'valid for 24 hours after initial issuance' (expires_in 86400); refresh tokens are 'valid for 365 days after the initial issuance' (refresh_expires_in 31536000). On refresh, 'The returned refresh_token may be different than the one passed in the payload. You must use the newly-returned token if the value is different than the previous one', so always overwrite the stored token. Revoke via POST open.tiktokapis.com/v2/oauth/revoke/.

Redirect URI rules are strict and platform-specific: Web URIs must be https, absolute, static (no query params or fragments), max 10; Desktop must use localhost/127.0.0.1 with a port (http allowed); iOS must be an Apple universal link with associated domains; Android must be an App Link or Deep Link. The redirect_uri at token exchange 'must be the same as the redirect_uri used for requesting code', and the code sent must be URL-decoded.

Users can grant a subset of scopes: 'Users can grant a subset of what you request'; the token response returns the actually-granted scope list, and users 'can revoke the authorization at any time on their TikTok apps'. Design features to degrade per-scope. The stable user identifier is open_id, scoped to your app; 'client secret and refresh token must live server-side only'.
Rate detail: the Content Posting Direct Post init endpoint allows '6 requests per minute' per user access token. A QR-code authorization variant also exists for desktop/TV-style contexts.

Legacy stack still exists: clients still on the old auth/authorize/ endpoint or old mobile SDKs use a legacy token guide; only apps using v2/auth/authorize/ use the current User Access Token Management API. Do not mix the two generations of documentation.
prerequisites: A TikTok developer account and (recommended) an organization
App details assets: icon (1024x1024 px, JPEG/JPG/PNG, up to 5 MB), name, category, description, official website URL
Verified Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs for production

steps.detail: Create a developer account from the signup page using your email, and create or join an organization ('highly recommended but not required'). Manage apps > Connect an app > select the app owner (organization); the app is created in Draft status and the app page issues the Client key and Client secret.
steps.title: Create the developer account; register the app

steps.detail: Icon (1024x1024 px, JPEG/JPG/PNG, up to 5 MB), app name, category, description (shown on the authorization page), and platform configuration (Web/Desktop: official website URL; Android: package name, Play Store URL, app signature and signing certificate; iOS: App Store URL and Bundle ID). Add products (e.g. Login Kit) with at least one redirect URI, and add scopes in the Scopes section (user.info.basic is added by default with Login Kit).
steps.title: Fill in App details; add products and scopes

steps.detail: Sandbox is a 'restricted environment that allows you to try out integrations without having to submit your app for review' (up to 5 sandboxes per app; up to 10 target-user accounts). Redirect the user to tiktok.com/v2/auth/authorize/ with client_key, scope, redirect_uri, state, response_type=code; verify state on return; exchange the code server-side at POST open.tiktokapis.com/v2/oauth/token/ (grant_type=authorization_code, client_key, client_secret, URL-decoded code, same redirect_uri); store access_token, refresh_token, and open_id on your back end.
steps.title: Build and test in Sandbox mode

steps.detail: Verify URL properties (Terms of Service URL, Privacy Policy URL, Web/Desktop URL, for apps created after September 9, 2024) via domain verification or by uploading the provided signature file. Import the sandbox configuration into a Production Draft ('Import... will overwrite the draft's existing configuration'), complete the App review section (per-product/scope explanations + demo video recorded in the sandbox, showing every selected product and scope), and click Submit for review.
steps.title: Verify URLs; submit for review

steps.detail: Run the same flow against production credentials for real users; refresh tokens server-side before expiry (access 24 hours, refresh 365 days); revoke via POST open.tiktokapis.com/v2/oauth/revoke/ on disconnect. Any later configuration change requires Create revision > edit the cloned Draft > submit for review again. If you post publicly, the Content Posting API audit is a further gate before posts can be public.
steps.title: Go Live; refresh and revoke

tagline: Everything is gated behind a human app review: the app sits in Draft and Sandbox (up to 10 target accounts) until a review with a mandatory sandbox-recorded demo video approves it as Live, and public posting needs a second audit on top. No review timeline or fees are published.

time.active: ~35 min of app setup + ~half a day of flow and sandbox work
time.total: Unknown: review duration is not stated
